frame_tolerance_s_reason: Preserve the camera loader's existing half-second tolerance for matching recorded frames and reject LiDAR scans farther than this from the thermal frame.
inspection_shape_min_points_reason: With 80 independent Gaussian range samples, RMS noise has about 8 percent relative standard error, below the existing 50 percent residual-above-noise margin. Eighty also matches the inspection plane segmenter minimum. Below the fractional coverage gate, require at least 20 real camera rays in each of the four image quadrants and a measured body-sized footprint. Four quadrants constrain both image axes; a surviving patch cannot certify the whole body. Correlation and mixed surfaces can violate the ideal noise model, so all negative recordings still need audit. Missing rays and planar LiDAR ranges never count as camera points. This is a fitting-support requirement, not a cutoff fitted to a recording.
inspection_min_depth_fraction_reason: Preserve inspect_candidate's existing 60 percent valid registered-depth gate. Below it, fill only missing warm-component pixels from a matching LiDAR scan before applying the same inspection checks.
bearing_tolerance_deg_reason: A 10 degree column band spans about 73 centre pixels at sensors.json camera.fx=415.692. Recorded A/B t=0 at bearing 0 contain doorway ceilings while bands at +/-30 and +/-35 contain facade walls. The same half-width limits frontier evidence reuse.
wall_side_offset_deg_reason: Adjacent 10 degree bands touch the central band without a gap. At the 640 pixel camera's 37.6 degree half horizontal view, central and side walls can be measured separately.
normal_offset_px_reason: Normals use endpoints 24 pixels apart. At 8 m and fx=415.692 this is a 0.462 m baseline, compared with sensors.json depth sigma=0.096 m. Recorded A/B t=0 facade bands yielded no overhead horizontal hits with this baseline; a 5 pixel OpenCV normal window yielded spurious hits at heights 1.815-1.858 m.
surface_tilt_tolerance_deg_reason: Recorded A/B t=0 doorway ceiling normals with the 24 pixel baseline have gravity dot products near 0.998-1.000; facade normals have 90th percentiles 0.066-0.073. A 15 degree cone admits the ceiling and rejects these vertical facades. Walls use the complementary cone.
overhead_clearance_m_reason: Require points above the 1.6 m mast by at least the depth sensor's 0.2 m minimum measurable distance. This excludes camera-height clutter without imposing a ceiling height band.
min_ceiling_upward_fraction_reason: With the 24 pixel normal baseline, recorded A/B t=0 central doorway ceiling shares are 0.356/0.301 and facade shares are zero. A t=120 has only 0.059 with this baseline; a 0.04 minimum retains narrow visible ceiling evidence while rejecting isolated normal errors. This is calibrated on these frames, not a universal indoor prior.
min_wall_fraction_reason: Recorded A t=0 centre wall share is about 0.025 with the 24 pixel baseline, and facade shares exceed 0.79. Require at least 0.02 in one of the three bands so overhead evidence alone does not accept an isolated canopy.
min_lower_return_fraction_reason: Recorded A/B t=0 doorway lower return shares are 0.685/0.686. Requiring a majority retains these entry views but leaves total sensor dropout unknown instead of calling it sky.
min_upward_void_fraction_reason: Recorded indoor B t=60 upward dropout is 0.486, and doorway B t=0 is 0.495. Requiring 0.9 prevents those measured dropout levels from being called outdoors. Open-sky analytic rays have share 1.0. Wall evidence keeps a range-limited high-ceiling view unknown even above this threshold.
pending_candidate_s_reason: While an agent is approaching an uncertain warm candidate, explore_frontier is refused for up to this long, so the robot finishes the approach and inspects again before searching on. Hidden-corner run 3: both agents ordered an approach and dropped it for a frontier on the next area_searched event 4 to 18 s later, and nobody was confirmed. The farthest inspection seen was 10.2 m; at the 0.3 m/s doorway speed that walk takes about 34 s, plus about 20 s for an agent step and a close inspection.
place_features_per_keyframe_reason: Dev sweep (hidden_run1+run3, cross pairs, zero false accepts): recall 5.8-8.8% at 48 features, 9.5-11.5% at 64, 14-17% at 96, 18-20% at 128. 96 features is 5+38*96=3653 bytes, below the existing 5.4 KB brain message; 48 (1829 bytes) stays an option by changing this key.
place_detect_features_reason: ORB detects 1000 per frame; median 530 keep valid depth within range, so the top 96 are chosen from a pool of several hundred. 2000 changed recall by under 2 points in the dev sweep.
place_min_features_reason: Below 24 usable features a keyframe cannot reach the 16 inliers needed. Rejected frames are mostly a wall closer than the depth sensor's 0.2 m minimum, where depth is invalid (see evaluation JSON).
place_max_depth_m_reason: Depth sigma is 1.5 mm/m^2 (sensors.json): 0.0375 m at 5 m, 0.096 m at 8 m. Dev recall was flat from 4.5 to 8 m and worse at 3 m (7.7% vs 12%), so 5 m drops the noisy far points at no cost.
place_ratio_test_reason: Dev sweep at 96 features: ratio 0.65/0.7/0.75/0.8 needed 5/5/6/10 inliers for zero false accepts; 0.75 kept the most recall near the lowest threshold.
place_ransac_threshold_m_reason: Paired depth noise of two features at the 5 m limit is 0.053 m (1 sigma); 0.1 m is about 2 sigma. Dev recall was identical for 0.05 to 0.15 m, while negatives with 2 or 3 chance inliers rose from 44 to 134 as it widened.
place_height_tolerance_m_reason: Height noise from depth error is at most 0.04 m per feature at 5 m, 0.057 m for a pair; 0.2 m is 3.5 sigma. Dev results were identical for 0.15 to 0.5 m.
place_min_inliers_reason: Chosen for zero wrong accepts in database mode over all three recordings (1142 queries). At 7 inliers pair mode had zero false accepts, but database mode on heldout_run1 accepted 8 wrong poses in a white-tile and checkerboard room; the worst had 15 inliers. 16 clears them at a cost in recall (see evaluation JSON).
place_max_rmse_m_reason: Inlier RMSE of correct dev matches: median 0.019 m, p95 0.042 m, max 0.058 m.
place_keyframes_kept_reason: A 200 s run sampled every second is 201 keyframes; 300 keeps a longer run. Matching 200 keyframes took 10 ms (measured); 300 keyframes use about 1.1 MB.
place_shortlist_reason: Dev database mode gave identical results for shortlists of 3, 5, 10 and 25.
place_ransac_iterations_reason: Matches per pair are under 40, so all C(n,2) pairs (at most 741) are tried when n is small; 500 random pairs otherwise.
place_ransac_seed_reason: Fixed so the same input always gives the same pose.
place_ransac_min_baseline_m_reason: Two matches closer than this fix rotation poorly (depth noise 0.05 m over 0.4 m is 7 degrees). Dev: 0.2 m raised false-accept inliers from 4 to 6; 0.8 m cost recall.
place_refine_iterations_reason: The inlier set stops changing after 2 or 3 refits; 5 is a cap.
place_worker_timeout_s_reason: Measured keyframe max 0.35 s and match 10 ms; 30 s covers worker spawn and a slow disk.
place_orb_scale_factor_reason: Dev sweep: scale 1.2 with 8 levels gave 11.9% recall at zero false accepts, 1.3-1.5 with 5-6 levels gave 15.6-17.3%. A coarser pyramid stops the same corner taking several of the 96 slots at adjacent levels.
place_orb_levels_reason: Paired with scale 1.5 (1.5 scale over 5 levels spans 5x); same dev sweep.
place_http_timeout_s_reason: Keyframe extraction measured at most 0.35 s and matching about 10 ms in tools/place_eval.py. A 2 s client deadline allows over five times the measured extraction time. The recorder polls asynchronously and continues after timeout; the worker process has its own 30 s recovery bound.
burning_surface_c_reason: Surface temperature the robot assumes for floor it measures burning: flaming wood and furniture char run about 500 to 700 C (fire-engineering handbook values); the middle is used. Only for the spray advice.
knockdown_c_reason: A burning surface cooled below about 300 C stops pyrolysing fast enough to keep a flame (piloted ignition of wood is about 300 to 350 C). The spray advice counts a fire as knocked down when its surface is cooled to this.
fuel_surface_kj_per_m2_k_reason: Heat stored per square metre per degree in the hot surface layer the water must cool: wood and char about 500 kg/m3 at about 1.6 kJ/kg K over the top 8 mm gives about 6.5 kJ/m2 K. Only for the spray advice.
burning_kw_per_m2_reason: Heat release the robot assumes per square metre of floor it measures burning: a burning rate of about 0.018 kg/m2/s for furniture and wood times about 18 MJ/kg heat of combustion (fire-engineering handbook values). Used only to judge whether its water can knock a blocking fire down.
floor_band_m_reason: Warm pixels within this height of the floor plane are floor, not a body, when inspect_candidate cuts out warm regions: a lying adult is 0.2 to 0.3 m thick, and floor heated by a fire glows in the human band (one-door seeds 922 and 923: people lying in front of a burning sofa merged with the warm floor into one fire-sized region and were judged not_person).
door_edge_low_reason: RGB gradient threshold about ten times the configured 2/255 pixel noise, to suppress noise contours. Estimate for visible seams, not calibrated on a house.
door_edge_high_reason: Canny strong-edge threshold about thirty times the configured 2/255 pixel noise. Weak connected seams use door_edge_low.
door_polygon_fraction_reason: Allow contour simplification error of two percent of its perimeter for image sampling and perspective. A convex four-corner panel is still required.
door_min_width_m_reason: Broad lower bound for a service-door leaf. A candidate narrower than the robot still does not become passable.
door_max_width_m_reason: Broad bound covering paired access panels; larger rectangles are treated as unclassified walls. This is an object-shape prior, not a house type or room list.
door_min_height_m_reason: Reject small cabinets and pictures. Low service doors can be missed; size alone never certifies a door.
door_max_height_m_reason: Broad access-panel size bound. Taller panels remain unknown rather than imposing a ceiling height.
door_bottom_max_height_m_reason: A traversable doorway reaches within a body-step-sized quarter metre of the floor. A higher sill is a window or panel candidate, not a door.
door_min_valid_fraction_reason: Require measured depth over most of the panel. Missing returns never stand in for a door leaf.
door_plane_fraction_reason: At least ninety percent of measured panel depth must lie on one plane; the remainder permits a handle and narrow edge registration errors.
door_plane_noise_sigma_reason: Three depth-noise standard deviations, using sensors.json sigma coefficient times range squared, bound plane and recess evidence.
door_plane_floor_m_reason: Eight millimetres accommodates depth quantization, thin trim and plane-fit numerical error at close range.
door_plane_refits_reason: Initial PCA fit, outlier rejection and two refits. Deterministic bounded computation; no scene-specific sampling seed.
door_recess_min_m_reason: A leaf at least two centimetres behind surrounding trim supplies a separate geometric cue, only if larger than the depth-noise bound.
door_handle_min_protrusion_m_reason: A handle must project at least two centimetres in front of the fitted leaf and exceed its depth-noise bound.
door_handle_max_protrusion_m_reason: A protrusion beyond eighteen centimetres is more consistent with clutter than a knob or lever.
door_handle_min_width_m_reason: Two centimetres is a small knob or the resolved part of a lever; smaller components are depth speckle.
door_handle_max_width_m_reason: Broad upper bound for a lever and its backplate.
door_handle_min_height_m_reason: Minimum resolved handle thickness of fifteen millimetres.
door_handle_max_height_m_reason: Allow a knob and backplate, reject broad foreground objects.
door_handle_edge_fraction_reason: A handle is normally near a free vertical panel edge. Keep only the outer thirty-five percent on either side; hinge and swing direction remain unknown.
rgb_clipped_min_confidence_reason: A colour person box cut by the image side still confirms at this confidence or more when it is also wide (rgb_clipped_min_width_fraction). Owner, 24 Oct: verification too rigid. Three seed 934 runs: 27 inspections aimed at real people, 21 person verdicts; a 0.67 box cut by the side was one of the misses. Held-out seed 914: a 22 px sliver at 0.58 confirmed a false person, so it stays out.
rgb_clipped_min_width_fraction_reason: A side-cut box must be at least a sixth of the image wide to stand for a body; the false 914 sliver was 22 of 640 px (3 %).
rgb_side_margin_px_reason: Integer conversion of decoded box edges loses up to one pixel. A box ending in the last pixel cannot establish an unclipped side contour.
fusion_memory_s_reason: Bound stationary-body association to one minute so accumulated localisation drift and changed fire conditions do not persist for the mission.
fusion_association_m_reason: A partial view can measure another part of a torso up to about 0.3 m away; allow that extent in both observations. This is not a house coordinate or truth-match radius.
fusion_view_baseline_m_reason: A quarter-metre translation is one robot body radius and changes the depth rays used for corroboration. Rotation alone is the same viewpoint.
fusion_min_interval_s_reason: Require at least half a second between supporting views, rather than counting adjacent frames of one sensor exposure.
fusion_temperature_change_c_reason: Permit a few degrees of apparent-temperature change from clothing, view angle and smoke. Greater change does not corroborate a stable thermal body.
fusion_min_views_reason: Require two translated observations, each independently passing thermal structure and measured depth-shape checks. Neither needs an unclipped silhouette.
fusion_max_observations_reason: Bound per-robot storage to 128 small evidence records. This covers sixty seconds at two separated observations per second with eight records spare.
rgb_lidar_min_beams_reason: Require three consecutive half-degree scanner rays inside the colour box. At 12 m their one-degree total span covers about 0.21 m, smaller than an adult torso; an isolated range cannot place the visual person.
rgb_lidar_span_m_reason: The rays supporting one colour detection must agree within 0.3 m, approximately torso thickness. This rejects mixtures of furniture and a wall behind the box. LiDAR supplies range only; colour confidence and confirmation range checks still apply.
face_turns_per_spot_reason: Turns in place an agent may order toward one spot (1.5 m cell) within face_memory_s. The first brings a clipped body into view; a second covers a mis-measured bearing; a third from the same place adds no view. Seed 932: robot A ordered face, approach, face, face at one wall patch in 4 s (58.7 to 62.8 s) and robot B ordered 6 faces at two wall patches between 59.8 and 94 s; over the nine one-door runs 32 of 164 face orders completed within 0.1 s because the robot already faced the point.
face_memory_s_reason: How long face turns at a spot are remembered, the same as the close-look memory (ToolRegistry.LOOK_MEMORY_S, 90 s): long against the 4 to 7 s between agent steps, short against a run, so a spot seen again later from elsewhere gets fresh turns.
person_onnx_reason: The colour person detector run by OpenCV 5 cv2.dnn (file under data/models/onnx), 1266 ms per frame on the M5 CPU. yolo26s (367 ms) was measured on 23 Oct 2026 over 1212 recorded frames (729 visible-person views, 69 people, 500 negatives; boxes matched to projected footprints, a proxy) through the same cv2.dnn path: equal in aggregate (view recall 0.427 against 0.443, live-rule candidates 34 against 33 of 69, 0.020 against 0.024 false boxes per negative frame at conf 0.25) but it misses recorded people that yolo11m sees (seeds 924 A 38 s and 925 A 48 s, both regression tests), and per-person recall is lower (0.638 against 0.681). People found outrank speed, so yolo11m stays. yolo26n (111 ms): view recall 0.171, rejected.
two_view_max_range_m_reason: A person verdict seen from beyond person_confirm_max_range_m (5.0 m) may be confirmed only by two agreeing views, each within this range: the depth camera's maximum range (sensors.json depth.max_m 8.0), beyond which no body range is measured. Measured over the nine one-door recordings: every real person with a person verdict who was never confirmed (926 s3, 927 s6, 928 s2, 928 s3, 929 s1) was seen only from 5.1 to 8.4 m, with position errors of 0.06 to 0.40 m; one long view (928 B, 5.4 m) was 1.53 m off, so a single long view is not enough.
two_view_agree_m_reason: The two views' measured positions must agree within this distance, and the confirmed position is their mean. Single long views of real people were 0.06 to 0.40 m from truth (n = 7), so two good views agree within 0.5 m while a 1.53 m outlier does not. Offline over all logged inspections and the audit's sampled camera calls of runs 922 to 929 and 932 (143 view pairs within fusion_memory_s): 8 confirmations of 5 distinct people, all within 1.05 m of truth, 0 false. The non-person side is a small sample (tens of person verdicts on non-person components), so this is directional.
two_view_baseline_m_reason: The two standpoints must be at least this far apart, twice fusion_view_baseline_m (one body radius): views from one spot share the same ray geometry and range error, so their agreement proves nothing. With 1.0 m the same offline check confirmed 2 of the 5 people, with 0.5 m all 5, both with 0 false.
